headline: Who owns the water: Chennai's allocation ledger
intro: Chennai's water rests on paper signed far from the city: a 1976 agreement in which three other states each spared 5 TMC of Krishna water for Madras, a 1983 accord that set 12 TMC a year at the Tamil Nadu border, with receipts below that figure in most years since 1996. This ledger shows what each arrangement promises, what actually arrives, and how solid the paper is.
unit_note: Inter-state entitlements are in TMC per year (thousand million cubic feet; 1 TMC is about 28.3 billion litres - 12 TMC/yr is roughly 931 MLD). Plant capacities are in MLD.

authorities.name: Government of Andhra Pradesh (Telugu Ganga system)
authorities.role: Operates the canal chain that carries Chennai's Krishna water: Srisailam reservoir to Somasila to Kandaleru, then the 152 km Kandaleru-Poondi canal to the Tamil Nadu border.
authorities.capacity: 12 TMC/yr net due at the border
authorities.tension: Receipts have been below the 12 TMC figure in most years since 1996, roughly 2-3 TMC in recent years. In wet years Chennai suspends intake when its reservoirs are full, so part of the difference reflects the city's own intake decisions.

authorities.name: CMWSSB (as contract counterparty)
authorities.role: Chennai's water utility. Beyond operating the city system, it has been the buyer under long-term desalination contracts. It bought the privately built Minjur plant's output under a 25-year bulk-water purchase from 2010; CMWSSB issued a termination order on 24.09.2024 and, under Madras High Court orders, has operated the plant since 01.04.2025, refurbishing it towards an interim 20 MLD (MAWS Policy Note 2026-27, pp.194-195).
authorities.tension: Desalination is the one entitlement Chennai fully controls - no other state signs it - and the city is adding more of it (350 MLD built, 400 more under construction), though it is the costliest water in the ledger. CMWSSB's Contingency Plan 2026 and the MAWS Policy Note 2026-27 count Nemmeli I at 110 MLD, 360 MLD in all.

events.title: The 5-TMC-each understanding
events.note: The riparian states first agree in principle to spare 5 TMC each of Krishna water for Madras - thirteen years before it becomes paper.

events.title: Tripartite agreement signed (15 TMC)
events.note: Maharashtra, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh jointly sign on 14 April 1976 to spare 15 TMC of Krishna water for Chennai city.

events.title: AP-TN accord: 12 TMC net at the border
events.note: The implementation accord of 18 April 1983 sets the operative promise - 15 TMC drawn at Srisailam, 12 net at the Tamil Nadu border after en-route losses, in two seasonal spells.

events.title: First Krishna water reaches Poondi
events.note: Water first arrives in September 1996, thirteen years after the accord.

futures.status: Under construction (JICA-funded, Rs 5,814.57 crore); the state expects completion and commissioning by October 2027 - would take desalination to 750 MLD (760 MLD with Nemmeli I counted at 110), the largest single entitlement Chennai fully controls

gaps: No public year-wise series of Krishna water actually realised at the border since 1996 - the receipt record here is stitched from per-year press quoting WRD officials. The full series likely sits in TN WRD or CMWSSB policy notes.
The 1976 and 1983 agreement texts are not online in primary form; the entitlement wording rests on CMWSSB's official paraphrase.
The seasonal spell split is reported variously as July-October and June-October for the 8 TMC spell; CMWSSB's Contingency Plan 2026 (p.3) gives July to October.
